official.title: Postdoctoral Research Fellow
official.description_text:
We are looking for a
Postdoctoral Research Fellow
to work on deep learning methodologies for machine and robot perception.
The position is funded by the Horizon Europe project OPERA (Open Perception, Learning, and Decision-Making Toolbox for General Purpose Robot AI), and the selected applicant will be a member of the Signal Analysis and Machine Intelligence group led by Professor
Moncef Gabbouj
, and closely collaborate with the Machine Intelligence group led by Professor
Alexandros Iosifidis
, on achieving the goals and objectives of Tampere University team within the project.
The position is full-time starting from November 1
st
, 2026, until the end of the project September 30
th
, 2030. In case a selected applicant starts later than the start of the project, the duration of the position will be adjusted to end at the end of the project. The position is placed in the
Unit of Computing Sciences
within Tampere University's
Faculty of Information Technology and Communication Sciences
. The workplace is located at Hervanta Campus of Tampere University, Finland.
JOB DESCRIPTION
The postdoctoral researcher fellow at Tampere University will propose and develop novel deep learning methodologies, disseminate their results in high-quality publications in international conferences and journals, interact with project partners in project activities, integrate their methodologies and related baselines to the toolbox of the project. The selected postdoctoral researcher fellow will also be responsible for the project deliverables related to the tasks below, arranging and attending period meetings with the researchers in the team and in the consortium, publishing high-quality papers in relevant conferences and journals. The research topics for the selected applicant are the following:
Efficient human-centric active perception and learning
Social signal analysis and collaborative learning
Learning for increased robustness to variations and adaptation
Active sensor fusion for increased robustness and adaptivity
In addition, the duties of the postdoctoral researcher fellow may include some teaching tasks (5-10 %) in topics connected to their expertise.
REQUIREMENTS
A completed doctoral degree in computer science, computer engineering, or another related field
Proven expertise in Machine Learning theory and methods, and related Deep Learning approaches
Excellent knowledge of programming in Python and scientific libraries used for Deep Learning (PyTorch or TensorFlow). Ability to work using multiple Deep Learning libraries
Ability to pursue independent scholarly activity and lead systematic scientific research related to the design of Deep Learning methods and models
A curious mind and solid skills in critical thinking and problem solving
Very good communication skills in English, and ability to lead and collaborate in multidisciplinary teams
Ability to write research papers in high-quality peer-reviewed journals or conferences in the field of Machine Learning and Computer Vision
WE OFFER
The full-time position will be filled for a fixed-term period
starting from November 1
st
, 2026 until the end of the project September 30
th
, 2030
. In case a selected applicant starts later than the start of the project, the duration of the position will be adjusted to end at the end of the project.
The salary will be based on both the job requirements and the employee’s personal performance in accordance
with the Finnish University Salary System
. According to the criteria applied to teaching and research staff, the position of a postdoctoral researcher fellow is placed on level 5 of the job requirements scale. A typical starting salary for a postdoctoral researcher fellow is 4000-4200 EUR/month. The salary increases based on performance.
As a member of staff at Tampere University, you will enjoy a range of competitive benefits, such as occupational health care services, flexible work schedule, versatile research infrastructure, modern teaching facilities and a safe and inviting campus area as well as a personal fund to spend on sports and cultural activities in your free time. Please read more about
working at Tampere University
. You can also find more information about us and working and living Tampere by watching our video:
Tampere Higher Education Community - our academic playground
.
Tampere is one of the major academic hubs in the Nordic countries and offers a dynamic living environment. Tampere region is one of Finland's three most rapidly growing urban areas and home to a vibrant knowledge-intensive entrepreneurial community. The city is an industrial powerhouse that enjoys a rich cultural scene and a reputation as a centre of Finland’s information society.
Read more about Finland and Tampere:
Visit Finland
This is Finland
Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment: Welcome to Finland
Visit Tampere
HOW TO APPLY
Please submit your application through our online recruitment system.
The closing date for applications is Monday, October 12
th
, 2026 (at 23:59 EEST / UTC +3).
Please submit your application and all the accompanying documentation in English and attach them in PDF format.
Please attach only the following documents to your application:
Curriculum vitae
Free-form application letter including 1) a brief statement of how you meet the criteria for this position, and 2) description of your research interests in the scope of the postdoctoral researcher fellow position described above.
This letter should be max. 2 pages long, font 12.
List of publications
PDF copies of your Doctorate, Master’s and Bachelor’s degree certificates, including transcripts of all university records (in Finnish or English).
Other relevant documents that support your application, e.g. your doctoral thesis, the most relevant publications regarding the call (max. 4). Please include a list of 3 referees.
For more information, please contact:
Professor Moncef Gabbouj,
moncef.gabbouj@tuni.fi
Professor Alexandros Iosifidis,
alexandros.iosifidis@tuni.fi

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position in deep learning for machine and robot perception, part of the Horizon Europe OPERA project. Focus on efficient human-centric active perception, social signal analysis, collaborative learning, and sensor fusion for robotic systems through 2030.

thematic_fit.rationale: Partial thematic overlap on 'collaborative learning' and 'social signal analysis,' but core mission is pure robotics perception and ML algorithm development. Position is not about human-centered immersive systems, spatial cognition, or learning transfer—it is about robot autonomy and perception efficiency. 'Human-centric' refers to human-robot interaction perception, not human-centered research methodology or spatial/collaborative learning outcomes.

methodological_fit.rationale: Moderate methodological adjacency. Both involve designing for collaborative interaction and analyzing user/agent behavior. Candidate has intermediate user-studies and quantitative-research methods. However, position requires pure deep learning (PyTorch/TensorFlow) with no user studies or qualitative methods mentioned. Candidate would need to pivot from HCI methodology to ML engineering. The 'social signal analysis' and 'collaborative learning' topics could theoretically leverage user-study experience, but position framing emphasizes algorithm development over human outcomes.

growth_value.rationale: Developing deep learning and sensor-fusion skills would expand technical capability, but misaligned with target identity. Position does not advance spatial cognition, immersive-systems design, or human-centered evaluation. Work on 'collaborative learning' is algorithms-focused (how robots learn from collaborative tasks), not human-learning focused (how humans learn from collaboration). Would create capability in robotics/perception but not in target research domain.

strategic_value.rationale: Tampere University is priority-2 (acceptable but not priority). Horizon Europe funding is stable and prestigious. However, OPERA project is robotics/perception-driven; Signal Analysis and Machine Intelligence group and Machine Intelligence group (Gabbouj, Iosifidis) are pure ML/computer-vision labs with no HCI or immersive-systems focus. No clear pathway to XR/spatial-learning research from robotics perception.

eligibility_flags: Position is postdoc; candidate holds MSc by Research (in progress). Candidate is not yet eligible—PhD required. However, if candidate completes PhD by late 2026, this could become eligible for reapplication in 2027.
Position start is November 1, 2026; candidate is currently in thesis stage. PhD completion timeline uncertain; likely too tight unless accelerated.

Requires 'excellent knowledge of programming in Python and scientific libraries used for Deep Learning (PyTorch or TensorFlow). Candidate lists Python as beginner with no substantial project experience; significant skill gap.
risks: Eligibility barrier: Candidate is pre-PhD. Position explicitly requires PhD. Current candidacy is not viable unless timeline is accelerated dramatically.
Skill gap: Deep learning with PyTorch/TensorFlow is core requirement; candidate has no demonstrated experience. Onboarding risk is high.
Research-community misalignment: Robotics perception and XR/spatial-learning communities have limited intersection. Publications and collaborations would not advance target-identity positioning.
Supervision fit: Gabbouj and Iosifidis are ML/computer-vision experts, not HCI or immersive-systems researchers. Limited mentorship in human-centered evaluation or spatial cognition.
